To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the immune response to hCGβ is dominated by IgG2a, and to a lesser extent IgG2b antibodies, and (2) this is a Th1‐type response.
DNA vaccination can induce B cell memory, but not a strong primary antibody response.
(i) DNA vaccination favours memory over effector B cell response and (ii) the memory generation occurs without an overt effector B cell or T cell response.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation of B cell memory by DNA vaccination.
developing an effective DNA vaccination strategy to induce a strong antibody response.
developing an efficient and safe method of vaccination.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

DNA vaccination with this particular vector is a very effective method for inducing a B cell memory response, but the response is not as strong as that produced with conventional immunization with protein in adjudvant.
DNA‐vaccination is a powerful tool in generating memory B cells and that this response can be elicited in the absence of a strong effector response.
DNA vaccination favours the generation of memory over effector B cell immunity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

DNA immunization can be an effective means to prime and boost B cells for a subsequent protein‐induced response, but it is not a particularly effective way of inducing an antibody response in the absence of a protein challenge.
DNA vaccination can induce memory responses, which are as efficient as those induced by protein immunization, and that these responses can be rapidly recalled by a subsequent protein challenge.
DNA vaccination is an effective means of inducing B cell memory and that this memory is of a different quality to the memory induced following protein immunization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DNA immunization can be used to generate memory responses in mice, which can subsequently be elicited by a protein boost.
, while it is possible to elicit an immune memory response with DNA vaccination, the immune response is qualitatively different from the immune response generated following protein immunization.
DNA vaccination can be an effective way to generate a memory response, even in the absence of a detectable effector response.
